question: Which native change and identity contracts should providers reuse for local, remote and reconnect behavior?
method: best-api-review/history-v2; Task full execution; Redesign from First Principles; Plite Plan and Plate Plan adoption; Benchmark composite proof; Maintain Workflow doctrine repair; Agent Native Reviewer closure audit
trigger: The user authorized execution of the full corrected collaboration lifetime plan after the adversarial defer review, then asked to complete all implementation, proof and ledger reconciliation work.
requirements: Keep Y.Doc, provider connection and provider-specific initial readiness resources app-owned; require explicit doc and initialReady inputs and grant seed authority only through an exclusive external decision.
Reject waiting/error document and shared-effect work before publication or history, and never expose ready until required selection publication succeeds.
Surface shared-effect import failure as stable admission error, retain unacknowledged work and recover exactly once through retry without losing accepted offline edits.
Preserve one private controller and compaction authority per Y.Doc namespace, reject incompatible duplicate ownership and arbitrate one awareness selection across exact mounted views.
Expose live collaboration behavior through api.yjs, delete provider lifecycle, read.yjs and update/transaction Yjs surfaces, and infer awareness and compaction methods only when configured.
Preserve canonical Yjs convergence, relative identity, named roots, authored shared effects, history and the independent public YjsUpdatePolicy custom-adapter job.
Provide exact Plite and Plate headless/React exports and prove source, emitted declaration, packed boundary, real-provider browser and balanced composite performance behavior.
evidenceReuse: Rechecked the current owner and consumer source captured by this record. Reused earlier source investigations and failed or order-confounded benchmark receipts only as historical design evidence. Final acceptance comes from the implemented native/Plate contracts, current emitted declarations and package boundaries, generated registry, real Hocuspocus and mounted browser paths, and the current seven-cohort composite benchmark. Doctrine and generated mirrors were revalidated after their source repair.
summary: Pursue and mark adopted. The collaboration lifetime redesign is implemented: apps own providers and readiness, the native binding owns admission and Yjs identity, Plate composes the binding without a second store, and view-bound presence lives under capability-inferred api.yjs. Provider commands, public lifecycle/controller internals, read.yjs and Yjs update/transaction APIs are deleted. Atomic readiness, retained retry, namespace/compaction ownership, exclusive seeding, exact-view arbitration, public declarations, real-provider browser behavior and all seven balanced performance cohorts pass.
alternatives: Delete native collaboration and rely on JSON snapshots or path broadcasts: reject because offline convergence, relative cursor identity, named roots, authored shared effects and collaborative history remain independent current jobs.

Keep the provider facade, duplicate Plate store and read/update Yjs groups while patching local errors: reject because it preserves transport, resource and live-state ownership under editor transaction lifetimes.

Export a generic Hocuspocus readiness/provider service: cut because provider construction, connection, seed grants and destruction are app resources and the current apps need concrete version-specific ownership.
Use one native Yjs binding with app-owned resources and a capability-inferred Plate presentation adapter: selected and implemented; it satisfies the required jobs with the fewest public owners.
proofLimits: Manual one-hour and production soaks were not run because repository guidance requires an explicit soak request. No release or publication is claimed. Focused collaboration proof is green; broader checkout commands still stop on concurrent authored/suggestion API-key drift, clipboard internal-export bookkeeping, a Plate media caption split, a table type-instantiation error and an authored/clipboard browser insertion-offset mismatch. The plan records each failure and the independently passing affected stages.
